memo.verdict: Neutral; park on price. AQ Group (AQ-SE) is a compounder bought late: the business is compelling, the investment at SEK 248.0 (2026-10-06) is not, because the 'Modal return' is about minus 1 percent a year over eighteen months and about 4 percent a year over three years against the 20 percent bar. Re-visit level about SEK 185 (the eighteen-month test); entry level about SEK 165 (both tests; the 52-week low); or sooner if a de-rating comes without a fundamental break. Conviction medium: the business judgement is firm, the multiple judgement rests on a 40/60 blend. The park rule does not bite (no D or F on management, business quality, predictability or trackability), so this is a valuation park; the case progresses to Early-Stage work on two questions (the data-centre customer's contract terms and design lock-in; the defence pipeline's size) when the price allows. Not bearish (estimates rising, momentum A and B, business sound); not bullish (the return is below the bar on every combination of the inputs' figures). Triaging stage, 2026-10-08.
case: The thesis: a proven, net-cash, decentralised engineered-components manufacturer has added a higher-margin product line for AI data centres, raised its structural margin standard and lifted organic growth to 9.1 percent, and at SEK 248.0 the shares already pay for all of that change and more.

The change is external and structural, and new to this company at scale. Two sector-level demand forces with two-plus years' visibility, medium-voltage transformers for hyperscale data centres (output doubled sequentially in Q2 2026 to 70 systems a month across Hungary, Finland, the US and the Czech Republic; the ABB HiPerGuard chain; data-centre inductive components from negligible in 2024 to 6 percent of sales) and European defence (SEK 60m invested in northern Sweden; UK defence sales doubled; nominations on large requests for proposals pending), have turned the company's own cycle from minus 6.9 percent organic (FY2024) to 9.1 percent (Q2 2026), volume-led not price-led. Nearshoring and domestic-sourcing rules are a tailwind; tariffs have had negligible direct impact; the USD 3.7m Wytheville expansion puts transformer output inside the US tariff wall. The limit: the structural niches are about 12 percent of sales and the other 88 percent faces a flat-to-weak industrial cycle, with heavy trucks and agricultural machinery a headwind and the Mexico and Plattsburgh wiring plants underutilised. Headwinds already in the base: input costs (copper above USD 14,000 a tonne in May 2026; steel up 36.7 percent year on year) passed through with a 3 to 6 month unhedged lag; currency (73 percent of sales non-SEK, no hedging; a SEK 267m headwind in 2025, SEK 113m in H1 2026, SEK 3m in Q2 2026); EU compliance inflation; the EU Steel Overcapacity Regulation (50 percent out-of-quota duties from 1 July 2026); Pillar II from 2027. Disruption is two-sided: 800V DC architecture (orders from 2028; 40 to 50 percent of the AI market by 2030 on DNB Carnegie's reading) could bypass component suppliers unless AQ is designed in, which it is working on with a leading chip-maker.

The change inside the company is an improvement of degree, not a transformation. Three internal forces are strong: the EBT margin target raised from 8 to above 10 percent on 14 July 2026 (a 25 percent lift in the structural ambition, with the quarter delivering 9.9 percent; no numeric near-term guidance exists, so the raise is a target, not a forecast); the entry into medium-voltage transformers for data centres (rated A, the strongest single internal force, carrying design responsibility and therefore the margin claim); and a standards programme with published KPIs (delivery precision 98 percent; inventory turns 3.5; quality 100 percent) whose measured outputs slipped in the latest quarter. Beside them: a new independent chairman and a materially changed board; a re-articulated strategy toward design responsibility and complex systems, the 24-division reorganisation and Monitor ERP standardisation; resumed but small M&A (Time24 for £1 against a plan of two to four factories a year and 5 percent acquired growth; acquisitions since 2019 at about 6 times EBITA; mdexx taken from minus 7 to plus 7 percent EBT within a year). No chief-executive change, no perimeter change, no balance-sheet utilisation (net cash rising), no buyback ever, a small progressive dividend (SEK 1.80 for 2025, up 12.5 percent). None of the screen's red flags is present. Price is not a change force: price was a very small component of Q2 2026 growth and on a par with or slightly below inflation; OEMs demand 3 to 5 percent annual productivity cuts; the margin comes from cost, mix and utilisation.
counter_case: The strongest case against is the Risks report's "false friend": AQ's record quarter is top-line growth concealing a deterioration in the business beneath it. Operating cash flow collapsed 90 percent during a record profit, to SEK 23m in Q2 2026 from SEK 232m a year earlier, and net working capital jumped from 28.7 to 32.0 percent of trailing revenue in one quarter. Inventory turns are 2.9 against a 3.5 target, a 17 percent miss, after SEK 185m of inventory write-downs in 2025 and SEK 10m of localised write-offs in India and Bulgaria from poor material planning. Delivery precision fell to 92.7 percent from 94.7 percent during the most important ramp in the company's history, exactly as it fell to 90 percent in 2022 and 92 percent in 2021 the last two times volume surged; the new data-centre transformers carried quality defects in late 2025 and Q4 2025 took quality provisions for historical design defects in Bulgaria. One customer is about half of the data-centre segment, so the growth story has a single point of failure. The 10 percent EBT margin is a ceiling: the bull broker called it "a peak level for contract manufacturers" before the raise and the bear report puts further structural margin upside under 100 basis points, because the company has no intellectual property, faces OEMs who demand 3 to 5 percent annual productivity cuts, dual-source and contract for convenience, and has never printed a full year above 9.6 percent EBT; Time24 dilutes; copper and steel are at highs with a 3 to 6 month unhedged lag. There is zero currency hedging on 73 percent of sales, a formal policy and an outlier against every hedged peer. Pay governance is below the peers': warrants without performance conditions, clawbacks or holding periods that survive termination, and a remuneration committee of the two founders alone. The multiple is 20 times EV/EBITA against a nine-year peer median of 10.6 times, "a behavioural finance anomaly" that leaves no margin of safety, and the sell-side itself says "fully charged, fairly valued" and "the market had already priced in the strong delivery". In this reading the margin is a cyclical peak inflated by a surge of high-margin data-centre deliveries, the working-capital build is the first sign the ramp is beyond the sites' capability, and fair value is SEK 140 (2027 sales SEK 9,000m, an 8 percent EBIT margin, 15 times EV/EBIT). The Risks report's own analysis of competing hypotheses has this profile winning.

At Building Block level the counter-cases are: on the 'Foundations', that these are the foundations of a cyclical contract manufacturer whose margins are at a structural peak and whose power structure is unchanged by its mix; on the 'Investment Setup', that this is a late-cycle 'Demand Inflection' story being bought at the top, with the compounding record as the wrapper, so the right setup is a clearing pattern after a de-rating; on the 'Investment Case', that the market is right to pay, because Sell-side Momentum A, Technical Momentum B and Thematic Fit/Momentum B are the market confirming a structural re-rating of a permanently improved mix, so the 97th percentile is the new fair range and a D is a valuation opinion overruling every other attribute.
triggers: - The Q3 2026 report on 15 October 2026 tests both multiple conditions at once: operating cash flow back above SEK 200m (alarm below SEK 100m; invalidate a second quarter below SEK 100m); delivery precision above 95 percent (alarm below 92 percent; invalidate below 90 percent); organic growth, with a print above 10 percent and a rising data-centre share moving the growth condition to probable; H2 2026 revenue needing about 12.8 percent growth on H2 2025 for the FY2026 consensus of SEK 9,938m; the first full Time24 quarter.

- The margin condition: two consecutive quarters above 10 percent EBT with delivery precision above 95 percent moves it to probable; a quarter below 9 percent on a volume-led cost squeeze moves it to possible; alarm below 9.0 percent for a quarter; invalidate below 8 percent (the Risks report's re-run threshold). Modal 9.6 percent FY2026, 9.9 percent FY2027, 10.1 percent FY2028.

- The growth condition: a European truck production cut (Volvo and Scania) or a plateau in the data-centre share moves it to possible; alarm a sequential fall in the data-centre share or construction-equipment orders turning down again; invalidate organic growth below zero for two quarters. Data-centre share modal rising toward 10 percent of sales by FY2028.

- The concentration risk: a loss or redesign at the customer that is about 50 percent of the data-centre segment invalidates; ABB Electrification's order commentary and 800V DC design wins and announcements are the series.
- The multiple: no alarm, because a fall is the modal case; re-visit about SEK 185, enter about SEK 165, or sooner if a de-rating comes without a fundamental break.
- Inventory write-downs above SEK 50m in a quarter invalidate; turns modal 3.1 by FY2026 against a 3.5 target.
